# Repository Guidelines

## Agent bootstrap

Before changing files, read `.ai/architecture.yaml`, `.ai/rules/common.md`, `.ai/service.yaml`, `.ai/commands.yaml`, `docs/README.md`, the relevant `.ai/workflows/*` workflow, and affected contracts. Capture `git status --short` and `git diff`, then run the canonical policy command `./scripts/check-agent-policy.sh`; stop fail-closed if it fails. Code, migrations, tests, and repository-owned documents are authoritative.

## Architecture invariants

- `internal/domain` owns content types and ports; `internal/usecase` owns catalog, hierarchy, access, task, import, and lifecycle behavior; adapters own HTTP, PostgreSQL, NATS, FileStorage, and Task Answer details.
- This service owns authored course content and reusable catalog structure. Student answers, attempts, review, and progress remain owned by the student service.
- Preserve the authored hierarchy and order: track -> level -> course group -> course -> module -> section -> lesson -> task. Reusable entities and relation rows are separate concerns.
- Task type, capability fields, `code_structure`, assessment rows, compose/runtime configuration, and starter files form one contract. Update them atomically and keep the runtime consumers compatible.
- Public content visibility and inherited lesson read access are security-sensitive. Administrative header identity and internal shared tokens are current trust-boundary assumptions, not cryptographic authentication.
- Lifecycle events are compatibility contracts. Publish only after successful persistence; import transactions defer events until commit.
- Stable `source_key` identities and deterministic knowledge-import IDs must remain idempotent.
- Transport layout is fail-closed: direct children of `internal/transport` are limited to `http`, `message`, `cli`, `websocket`, and `common`; direct children of `internal/transport/http` are limited to `api`, `admin`, and `private`.
- Public, admin, and private HTTP handlers and audience-specific helpers belong exclusively to `api/v1`, `admin/v1`, and `private` respectively. Routers must not import another contour's transport code.
- `internal/infrastructure` is outbound-only and fail-closed to `persistence/postgres`, `messaging/nats`, `http/taskanswer`, and `filestorage`; `internal/adapters` is forbidden.
- `internal/domain` and `internal/usecase` must not import transport, infrastructure, or framework implementations. Composition wiring belongs in `cmd/mc-course-service/main.go`.

## Verification and delivery

- Use `.ai/commands.yaml`. After edits, rerun `./scripts/check-agent-policy.sh` and every scope-relevant declared verification command. Report each exact command and exit status; failed, skipped, or missing required evidence forbids completion or review.
- HTTP, task, assessment, access, event, schema, seed, import, and migration changes require synchronized tests and owned contracts.
- Migrations, seeds, imports, FileStorage uploads, provider calls, services, and destructive stack commands require the approval stated in `.ai/commands.yaml`.
